entries.originalText: Now the faith which is in Christ confirms all these [admonitions].
entries.modernizedText: Now the faith that is in Christ confirms all these [admonitions].

entries.originalText: For He Himself by the Holy Ghost thus addresses us: “Come, ye children, hearken unto me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
entries.modernizedText: For He Himself, through the Holy Spirit, addresses us thus: “Come, you children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.

entries.originalText: What man is he that desireth life, and loveth to see good days?
entries.modernizedText: What man is there who desires life and loves to see good days?

entries.originalText: Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile.
entries.modernizedText: Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit.

entries.originalText: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
entries.modernizedText: Depart from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.

entries.originalText: The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are [open] unto their prayers.
entries.modernizedText: The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are [open] to their prayers.

entries.originalText: The face of the Lord is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth.
entries.modernizedText: The face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to cut off their remembrance from the earth.

entries.originalText: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard him, and delivered him out of all his troubles.”
entries.modernizedText: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard him and delivered him from all his troubles.”

entries.originalText: “Many are the stripes [appointed for] the wicked; but mercy shall compass those about who hope in the Lord.”
entries.modernizedText: “Many are the stripes [appointed for] the wicked, but mercy will surround those who hope in the Lord.”

entries.originalText: The all-merciful and beneficent Father has bowels [of compassion] towards those that fear Him, and kindly and lovingly bestows His favours upon those who come to Him with a simple mind.
entries.modernizedText: The all-merciful and beneficent Father has compassion for those who fear Him, and kindly and lovingly bestows His favors upon those who come to Him with a simple mind.

entries.originalText: Wherefore let us not be double-minded; neither let our soul be lifted up on account of His exceedingly great and glorious gifts.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore let us not be double-minded, nor let our soul be lifted up because of His exceedingly great and glorious gifts.

entries.originalText: Far from us be that which is written, “Wretched are they who are of a double mind, and of a doubting heart; who say, These things we have heard even in the times of our fathers; but, behold, we have grown old, and none of them has happened unto us;” Ye foolish ones! compare yourselves to a tree; take [for instance] the vine.
entries.modernizedText: Far from us be what is written, “Wretched are those who are double-minded and of a doubting heart, who say, These things we heard even in the days of our fathers; but, behold, we have grown old, and none of them has happened to us.” You foolish ones! Compare yourselves to a tree; take [for instance] the vine.

entries.originalText: First of all, it sheds its leaves, then it buds, next it puts forth leaves, and then it flowers; after that comes the sour grape, and then follows the ripened fruit.
entries.modernizedText: First it sheds its leaves, then it buds, next it puts forth leaves, and then it flowers; after that comes the sour grape, and then the ripened fruit.

entries.originalText: Ye perceive how in a little time the fruit of a tree comes to maturity.
entries.modernizedText: You perceive how in a short time the fruit of a tree comes to maturity.

entries.originalText: Of a truth, soon and suddenly shall His will be accomplished, as the Scripture also bears witness, saying, “Speedily will He come, and will not tarry;” and, “The Lord shall suddenly come to His temple, even the Holy One, for whom ye look.”
entries.modernizedText: Truly, soon and suddenly His will will be accomplished, as the Scripture also bears witness, saying, “He will come speedily and will not delay,” and, “The Lord will suddenly come to His temple, even the Holy One for whom you look.”

entries.originalText: Let us consider, beloved, how the Lord continually proves to us that there shall be a future resurrection, of which He has rendered the Lord Jesus Christ the first-fruits by raising Him from the dead.
entries.modernizedText: Let us consider, beloved, how the Lord continually proves to us that there will be a future resurrection, of which He has made the Lord Jesus Christ the firstfruits by raising Him from the dead.

entries.originalText: Let us contemplate, beloved, the resurrection which is at all times taking place.
entries.modernizedText: Let us contemplate, beloved, the resurrection that is taking place at all times.

entries.originalText: Day and night declare to us a resurrection.
entries.modernizedText: Day and night declare a resurrection to us.

entries.originalText: The night sinks to sleep, and the day arises; the day [again] departs, and the night comes on.
entries.modernizedText: The night sinks into sleep, and the day arises; the day [again] departs, and the night comes on.

entries.originalText: Let us behold the fruits [of the earth], how the sowing of grain takes place.
entries.modernizedText: Let us behold the fruits [of the earth], how grain is sown.

entries.originalText: The sower goes forth, and casts it into the ground, and the seed being thus scattered, though dry and naked when it fell upon the earth, is gradually dissolved.
entries.modernizedText: The sower goes forth and casts it into the ground, and the seed, thus scattered, though dry and bare when it falls upon the earth, is gradually dissolved.

entries.originalText: Then out of its dissolution the mighty power of the providence of the Lord raises it up again, and from one seed many arise and bring forth fruit.
entries.modernizedText: Then from its dissolution the mighty power of the Lord’s providence raises it up again, and from one seed many arise and bear fruit.

entries.originalText: Let us consider that wonderful sign [of the resurrection] which takes place in eastern lands, that is, in Arabia and the countries round about.
entries.modernizedText: Let us consider that wonderful sign [of the resurrection] that takes place in the eastern lands, that is, in Arabia and the surrounding countries.

entries.originalText: There is a certain bird which is called a phœnix.
entries.modernizedText: There is a certain bird called a phoenix.

entries.originalText: This is the only one of its kind, and lives five hundred years.
entries.modernizedText: It is the only one of its kind and lives for five hundred years.

entries.originalText: And when the time of its dissolution draws near that it must die, it builds itself a nest of frankincense, and myrrh, and other spices, into which, when the time is fulfilled, it enters and dies.
entries.modernizedText: When the time of its dissolution draws near and it must die, it builds itself a nest of frankincense, myrrh, and other spices, into which, when the time is fulfilled, it enters and dies.

entries.originalText: But as the flesh decays a certain kind of worm is produced, which, being nourished by the juices of the deed bird, brings forth feathers.
entries.modernizedText: But as the flesh decays, a certain kind of worm is produced, which, nourished by the juices of the dead bird, grows feathers.

entries.originalText: Then, when it has acquired strength, it takes up that nest in which are the bones of its parent, and bearing these it passes from the land of Arabia into Egypt, to the city called Heliopolis.
entries.modernizedText: Then, when it has grown strong, it takes up the nest containing the bones of its parent, and carrying them, passes from the land of Arabia into Egypt, to the city called Heliopolis.

entries.originalText: And, in open day, flying in the sight of all men, it places them on the altar of the sun, and having done this, hastens back to its former abode.
entries.modernizedText: In broad daylight, flying in the sight of all, it places them on the altar of the sun, and having done this, hastens back to its former abode.

entries.originalText: The priests then inspect the registers of the dates, and find that it has returned exactly as the five hundredth year was completed.
entries.modernizedText: The priests then inspect the date registers and find that it returned exactly as the five hundredth year was completed.

entries.originalText: Do we then deem it any great and wonderful thing for the Maker of all things to raise up again those that have piously served Him in the assurance of a good faith, when even by a bird He shows us the mightiness of His power to fulfil His promise?
entries.modernizedText: Do we then consider it any great and wonderful thing for the Maker of all things to raise up again those who have piously served Him in the assurance of good faith, when even through a bird He shows us the mightiness of His power to fulfill His promise?

entries.originalText: For [the Scripture] saith in a certain place, “Thou shalt raise me up, and I shall confess unto Thee”; and again, “I laid me down, and slept”; “I awaked, because Thou art with me;” and again, Job says, “Thou shalt raise up this flesh of mine, which has suffered all these things.”
entries.modernizedText: For [the Scripture] says in a certain place, “You will raise me up, and I will confess to You”; and again, “I lay down and slept”; “I awoke, because You are with me”; and again, Job says, “You will raise up this flesh of mine, which has suffered all these things.”

entries.originalText: Having then this hope, let our souls be bound to Him who is faithful in His promises, and just in His judgments.
entries.modernizedText: Having this hope, then, let our souls be bound to Him who is faithful in His promises and just in His judgments.

entries.originalText: He who has commanded us not to lie, shall much more Himself not lie; for nothing is impossible with God, except to lie.
entries.modernizedText: He who has commanded us not to lie will Himself much more not lie, for nothing is impossible with God except to lie.

entries.originalText: Let His faith therefore be stirred up again within us, and let us consider that all things are nigh unto Him.
entries.modernizedText: Let faith in Him therefore be stirred up again within us, and let us consider that all things are near to Him.

entries.originalText: By the word of His might He established all things, and by His word He can overthrow them.
entries.modernizedText: By the word of His might He established all things, and by His word He can overthrow them.

entries.originalText: “Who shall say unto Him, What hast thou done? or, Who shall resist the power of His strength?”
entries.modernizedText: “Who will say to Him, What have You done? Or, Who will resist the power of His strength?”

entries.originalText: When, and as He pleases, He will do all things, and none of the things determined by Him shall pass away.
entries.modernizedText: When and as He pleases, He will do all things, and none of the things determined by Him will pass away.

entries.originalText: All things are open before Him, and nothing can be hidden from His counsel.
entries.modernizedText: All things are open before Him, and nothing can be hidden from His counsel.

entries.originalText: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament showeth His handy-work.
entries.modernizedText: “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament shows His handiwork.

entries.originalText: Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night showeth knowledge.
entries.modernizedText: Day after day pours out speech, and night after night shows knowledge.

entries.originalText: And there are no words or speeches of which the voices are not heard.”
entries.modernizedText: And there are no words or speeches whose voices are not heard.”

entries.originalText: Since then all things are seen and heard [by God], let us fear Him, and forsake those wicked works which proceed from evil desires; so that, through His mercy, we may be protected from the judgments to come.
entries.modernizedText: Since all things are seen and heard [by God], let us fear Him and forsake those wicked works that proceed from evil desires, so that through His mercy we may be protected from the judgments to come.

entries.originalText: For whither can any of us flee from His mighty hand?
entries.modernizedText: For where can any of us flee from His mighty hand?

entries.originalText: Or what world will receive any of those who run away from Him?
entries.modernizedText: Or what world will receive anyone who runs away from Him?

entries.originalText: For the Scripture saith in a certain place, “Whither shall I go, and where shall I be hid from Thy presence?
entries.modernizedText: For the Scripture says in a certain place, “Where shall I go, and where shall I be hidden from Your presence?

entries.originalText: If I ascend into heaven, Thou art there; if I go away even to the uttermost parts of the earth, there is Thy right hand; if I make my bed in the abyss, there is Thy Spirit.”
entries.modernizedText: If I ascend into heaven, You are there; if I go away even to the farthest parts of the earth, Your right hand is there; if I make my bed in the abyss, Your Spirit is there.”

entries.originalText: Whither, then, shall anyone go, or where shall he escape from Him who comprehends all things?
entries.modernizedText: Where, then, can anyone go, or where can he escape from Him who comprehends all things?

entries.originalText: Let us then draw near to Him with holiness of spirit, lifting up pure and undefiled hands unto Him, loving our gracious and merciful Father, who has made us partakers in the blessings of His elect.
entries.modernizedText: Let us then draw near to Him with holiness of spirit, lifting up pure and undefiled hands to Him, loving our gracious and merciful Father, who has made us partakers in the blessings of His elect.

entries.originalText: For thus it is written, “When the Most High divided the nations, when He scattered the sons of Adam, He fixed the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.
entries.modernizedText: For thus it is written, “When the Most High divided the nations, when He scattered the sons of Adam, He fixed the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.

entries.originalText: His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord, and Israel the lot of His inheritance.
entries.modernizedText: His people Jacob became the portion of the Lord, and Israel the lot of His inheritance.

entries.originalText: And in another place [the Scripture] saith, “Behold, the Lord taketh unto Himself a nation out of the midst of the nations, as a man takes the first-fruits of his threshing-floor; and from that nation shall come forth the Most Holy.”
entries.modernizedText: And in another place [the Scripture] says, “Behold, the Lord takes for Himself a nation from the midst of the nations, as a man takes the firstfruits of his threshing floor; and from that nation will come forth the Most Holy.”

entries.originalText: Seeing, therefore, that we are the portion of the Holy One, let us do all those things which pertain to holiness, avoiding all evil-speaking, all abominable and impure embraces, together with all drunkenness, seeking after change, all abominable lusts, detestable adultery, and execrable pride.
entries.modernizedText: Since, therefore, we are the portion of the Holy One, let us do all those things that pertain to holiness, avoiding all evil-speaking, all abominable and impure embraces, together with all drunkenness, a desire for change, all abominable lusts, detestable adultery, and execrable pride.

entries.originalText: “For God,” [saith the Scripture], “resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble.”
entries.modernizedText: “For God,” [says the Scripture], “resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

entries.originalText: Let us cleave, then, to those to whom grace has been given by God.
entries.modernizedText: Let us cleave, then, to those to whom grace has been given by God.

entries.originalText: Let us clothe ourselves with concord and humility, ever exercising self-control, standing far off from all whispering and evil-speaking, being justified by our works, and not our words.
entries.modernizedText: Let us clothe ourselves with concord and humility, always exercising self-control, standing far from all whispering and evil-speaking, being justified by our works and not our words.

entries.originalText: For [the Scripture] saith, “He that speaketh much, shall also hear much in answer.
entries.modernizedText: For [the Scripture] says, “He who speaks much will also hear much in answer.

entries.originalText: And does he that is ready in speech deem himself righteous?
entries.modernizedText: And does he who is ready in speech consider himself righteous?

entries.originalText: Blessed is he that is born of woman, who liveth but a short time: be not given to much speaking.”
entries.modernizedText: Blessed is he who is born of woman and lives but a short time: do not give yourself to much speaking.”

entries.originalText: Let our praise be in God, and not of ourselves; for God hateth those that commend themselves.
entries.modernizedText: Let our praise be in God and not in ourselves, for God hates those who commend themselves.

entries.originalText: Let testimony to our good deeds be borne by others, as it was in the case of our righteous forefathers.
entries.modernizedText: Let others bear testimony to our good deeds, as was the case with our righteous forefathers.

entries.originalText: Boldness, and arrogance, and audacity belong to those that are accursed of God; but moderation, humility, and meekness to such as are blessed by Him.
entries.modernizedText: Boldness, arrogance, and audacity belong to those who are accursed by God, but moderation, humility, and meekness belong to those who are blessed by Him.

entries.originalText: Let us cleave then to His blessing, and consider what are the means of possessing it.
entries.modernizedText: Let us cleave, then, to His blessing and consider the means of possessing it.

entries.originalText: Let us think over the things which have taken place from the beginning.
entries.modernizedText: Let us think over the things that have taken place from the beginning.

entries.originalText: For what reason was our father Abraham blessed?
entries.modernizedText: For what reason was our father Abraham blessed?

entries.originalText: Was it not because he wrought righteousness and truth through faith?
entries.modernizedText: Was it not because he practiced righteousness and truth through faith?

entries.originalText: Isaac, with perfect confidence, as if knowing what was to happen, cheerfully yielded himself as a sacrifice.
entries.modernizedText: Isaac, with perfect confidence, as if knowing what was to happen, cheerfully offered himself as a sacrifice.

entries.originalText: Jacob, through reason of his brother, went forth with humility from his own land, and came to Laban and served him; and there was given to him the sceptre of the twelve tribes of Israel.
entries.modernizedText: Because of his brother, Jacob went forth humbly from his own land, came to Laban, and served him; and he was given the scepter of the twelve tribes of Israel.

entries.originalText: Whosoever will candidly consider each particular, will recognise the greatness of the gifts which were given by him.
entries.modernizedText: Whoever candidly considers each detail will recognize the greatness of the gifts that were given through him.

entries.originalText: For from him have sprung the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God.
entries.modernizedText: For from him have come the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God.

entries.originalText: From him also [was descended] our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh.
entries.modernizedText: From him also [was descended] our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh.

entries.originalText: From him [arose] kings, princes, and rulers of the race of Judah.
entries.modernizedText: From him [arose] kings, princes, and rulers of the race of Judah.

entries.originalText: Nor are his other tribes in small glory, inasmuch as God had promised, “Thy seed shall be as the stars of heaven.”
entries.modernizedText: Nor are his other tribes without great glory, since God had promised, “Your seed will be like the stars of heaven.”

entries.originalText: All these, therefore, were highly honoured, and made great, not for their own sake, or for their own works, or for the righteousness which they wrought, but through the operation of His will.
entries.modernizedText: All these, therefore, were highly honored and made great, not for their own sake, their own works, or the righteousness they practiced, but through the working of His will.

entries.originalText: And we, too, being called by His will in Christ Jesus, are not justified by ourselves, nor by our own wisdom, or understanding, or godliness, or works which we have wrought in holiness of heart; but by that faith through which, from the beginning, Almighty God has justified all men; to whom be glory for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: And we, too, being called by His will in Christ Jesus, are not justified by ourselves, nor by our own wisdom, understanding, godliness, or works that we have practiced in holiness of heart, but by that faith through which, from the beginning, Almighty God has justified all people; to Him be glory forever and ever.

entries.originalText: What shall we do, then, brethren?
entries.modernizedText: What shall we do, then, brethren?

entries.originalText: Shall we become slothful in well-doing, and cease from the practice of love?
entries.modernizedText: Shall we become lazy in doing good and cease practicing love?

entries.originalText: God forbid that any such course should be followed by us!
entries.modernizedText: God forbid that we should follow such a course!

entries.originalText: But rather let us hasten with all energy and readiness of mind to perform every good work.
entries.modernizedText: Rather, let us hasten with all energy and readiness of mind to perform every good work.

entries.originalText: For the Creator and Lord of all Himself rejoices in His works.
entries.modernizedText: For the Creator and Lord of all Himself rejoices in His works.

entries.originalText: For by His infinitely great power He established the heavens, and by His incomprehensible wisdom He adorned them.
entries.modernizedText: For by His infinitely great power He established the heavens, and by His incomprehensible wisdom He adorned them.

entries.originalText: He also divided the earth from the water which surrounds it, and fixed it upon the immovable foundation of His own will.
entries.modernizedText: He also divided the earth from the water that surrounds it and fixed it upon the immovable foundation of His own will.

entries.originalText: The animals also which are upon it He commanded by His own word into existence.
entries.modernizedText: The animals that are upon it He also commanded into existence by His own word.

entries.originalText: So likewise, when He had formed the sea, and the living creatures which are in it, He enclosed them [within their proper bounds] by His own power.
entries.modernizedText: Likewise, when He had formed the sea and the living creatures that are in it, He enclosed them [within their proper bounds] by His own power.

entries.originalText: Above all, with His holy and undefiled hands He formed man, the most excellent [of His creatures], and truly great through the understanding given him—the express likeness of His own image.
entries.modernizedText: Above all, with His holy and undefiled hands He formed man, the most excellent [of His creatures], and truly great through the understanding given to him—the exact likeness of His own image.

entries.originalText: For thus says God: “Let us make man in our image, and after our likeness.
entries.modernizedText: For thus says God: “Let us make man in our image and after our likeness.

entries.originalText: So God made man; male and female He created them.”
entries.modernizedText: So God made man; male and female He created them.”

entries.originalText: Having thus finished all these things, He approved them, and blessed them, and said, “Increase and multiply.”
entries.modernizedText: Having thus finished all these things, He approved and blessed them, and said, “Increase and multiply.”

entries.originalText: We see, then, how all righteous men have been adorned with good works, and how the Lord Himself, adorning Himself with His works, rejoiced.
entries.modernizedText: We see, then, how all righteous men have been adorned with good works, and how the Lord Himself, adorning Himself with His works, rejoiced.

entries.originalText: Having therefore such an example, let us without delay accede to His will, and let us work the work of righteousness with our whole strength.
entries.modernizedText: Having such an example, therefore, let us without delay submit to His will, and let us do the work of righteousness with all our strength.

entries.originalText: The good servant receives the bread of his labour with confidence; the lazy and slothful cannot look his employer in the face.
entries.modernizedText: The good servant receives the bread of his labor with confidence; the lazy and slothful cannot look his employer in the face.

entries.originalText: It is requisite, therefore, that we be prompt in the practice of well-doing; for of Him are all things.
entries.modernizedText: It is necessary, therefore, that we be prompt in practicing well-doing, for all things are from Him.

entries.originalText: And thus He forewarns us: “Behold, the Lord [cometh], and His reward is before His face, to render to every man according to his work.”
entries.modernizedText: And thus He forewarns us: “Behold, the Lord [comes], and His reward is before Him, to render to every person according to his work.”

entries.originalText: He exhorts us, therefore, with our whole heart to attend to this, that we be not lazy or slothful in any good work.
entries.modernizedText: He exhorts us, therefore, with our whole heart to attend to this, so that we are not lazy or slothful in any good work.

entries.originalText: Let our boasting and our confidence be in Him.
entries.modernizedText: Let our boasting and our confidence be in Him.

entries.originalText: Let us submit ourselves to His will.
entries.modernizedText: Let us submit ourselves to His will.

entries.originalText: Let us consider the whole multitude of His angels, how they stand ever ready to minister to His will.
entries.modernizedText: Let us consider the whole multitude of His angels, how they always stand ready to minister to His will.

entries.originalText: For the Scripture saith, “Ten thousand times ten thousand stood around Him, and thousands of thousands ministered unto Him, and cried, Holy, holy, holy, [is] the Lord of Sabaoth; the whole creation is full of His glory.”
entries.modernizedText: For the Scripture says, “Ten thousand times ten thousand stood around Him, and thousands of thousands ministered to Him, and cried, Holy, holy, holy, [is] the Lord of Sabaoth; the whole creation is full of His glory.”

entries.originalText: And let us therefore, conscientiously gathering together in harmony, cry to Him earnestly, as with one mouth, that we may be made partakers of His great and glorious promises.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, conscientiously gathering together in harmony, let us cry to Him earnestly, as with one mouth, so that we may be made partakers of His great and glorious promises.

entries.originalText: For [the Scripture] saith, “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which He hath prepared for them that wait for Him.”
entries.modernizedText: For [the Scripture] says, “Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor have the things that He has prepared for those who wait for Him entered into the heart of man.”

entries.originalText: How blessed and wonderful, beloved, are the gifts of God!
entries.modernizedText: How blessed and wonderful, beloved, are the gifts of God!

entries.originalText: Life in immortality, splendour in righteousness, truth in perfect confidence, faith in assurance, self-control in holiness!
entries.modernizedText: Life in immortality, splendor in righteousness, truth in perfect confidence, faith in assurance, self-control in holiness!

entries.originalText: And all these fall under the cognizance of our understandings [now]; what then shall those things be which are prepared for such as wait for Him?
entries.modernizedText: And all these are within our understanding [now]; what, then, will those things be that are prepared for those who wait for Him?

entries.originalText: The Creator and Father of all worlds, the Most Holy, alone knows their amount and their beauty.
entries.modernizedText: The Creator and Father of all worlds, the Most Holy, alone knows their measure and beauty.

entries.originalText: Let us therefore earnestly strive to be found in the number of those that wait for Him, in order that we may share in His promised gifts.
entries.modernizedText: Let us therefore earnestly strive to be found among those who wait for Him, so that we may share in His promised gifts.

entries.originalText: But how, beloved, shall this be done?
entries.modernizedText: But how, beloved, shall this be done?

entries.originalText: If our understanding be fixed by faith towards God; if we earnestly seek the things which are pleasing and acceptable to Him; if we do the things which are in harmony with His blameless will; and if we follow the way of truth, casting away from us all unrighteousness and iniquity, along with all covetousness, strife, evil practices, deceit, whispering, and evil-speaking, all hatred of God, pride and haughtiness, vain glory and ambition.
entries.modernizedText: If our understanding is fixed by faith toward God; if we earnestly seek the things that are pleasing and acceptable to Him; if we do the things that are in harmony with His blameless will; and if we follow the way of truth, casting away from us all unrighteousness and iniquity, along with all covetousness, strife, evil practices, deceit, whispering, and evil-speaking, all hatred of God, pride and haughtiness, vainglory, and ambition.

entries.originalText: For they that do such things are hateful to God; and not only they that do them, but also those that take pleasure in them that do them.
entries.modernizedText: For those who do such things are hateful to God, and not only those who do them but also those who take pleasure in those who do them.

entries.originalText: For the Scripture saith, “But to the sinner God said, Wherefore dost thou declare my statutes, and take my covenant into thy mouth, seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee?
entries.modernizedText: For the Scripture says, “But to the sinner God said, Why do you declare my statutes and take my covenant into your mouth, since you hate instruction and cast my words behind you?

entries.originalText: When thou sawest a thief, thou consentedst with him, and didst make thy portion with adulterers.
entries.modernizedText: When you saw a thief, you consented with him and made your portion with adulterers.

entries.originalText: Thy mouth has abounded with wickedness, and thy tongue contrived deceit.
entries.modernizedText: Your mouth has abounded with wickedness, and your tongue contrived deceit.

entries.originalText: Thou sittest, and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.
entries.modernizedText: You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother’s son.

entries.originalText: These things thou hast done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest, wicked one, that I should be like to thyself.
entries.modernizedText: You have done these things, and I kept silent; you thought, wicked one, that I would be like you.

entries.originalText: But I will reprove thee, and set thyself before thee.
entries.modernizedText: But I will reprove you and set yourself before you.

entries.originalText: Consider now these things, ye that forget God, lest He tear you in pieces, like a lion, and there be none to deliver.
entries.modernizedText: Consider these things now, you who forget God, lest He tear you to pieces like a lion, with no one to deliver you.

entries.originalText: The sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and a way is there by which I will show him the salvation of God.”
entries.modernizedText: The sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is a way by which I will show him the salvation of God.”

entries.originalText: This is the way, beloved, in which we find our Saviour, even Jesus Christ, the High Priest of all our offerings, the defender and helper of our infirmity.
entries.modernizedText: This is the way, beloved, by which we find our Savior, Jesus Christ, the High Priest of all our offerings, the defender and helper of our weakness.

entries.originalText: By Him we look up to the heights of heaven.
entries.modernizedText: Through Him we look up to the heights of heaven.

entries.originalText: By Him we behold, as in a glass, His immaculate and most excellent visage.
entries.modernizedText: Through Him we behold, as in a mirror, His immaculate and most excellent face.

entries.originalText: By Him are the eyes of our hearts opened.
entries.modernizedText: Through Him the eyes of our hearts are opened.

entries.originalText: By Him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms up anew towards His marvellous light.
entries.modernizedText: Through Him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms anew toward His marvelous light.

entries.originalText: By Him the Lord has willed that we should taste of immortal knowledge, “who, being the brightness of His majesty, is by so much greater than the angels, as He hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.”
entries.modernizedText: Through Him the Lord has willed that we should taste immortal knowledge, “who, being the brightness of His majesty, is by so much greater than the angels, as He has by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.”

entries.originalText: For it is thus written, “Who maketh His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.”
entries.modernizedText: For it is thus written, “Who makes His angels spirits, and His ministers a flame of fire.”

entries.originalText: But concerning His Son the Lord spoke thus: “Thou art my Son, to-day have I begotten Thee.
entries.modernizedText: But concerning His Son the Lord spoke thus: “You are my Son; today I have begotten You.

entries.originalText: Ask of me, and I will give Thee the heathen for Thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for Thy possession.”
entries.modernizedText: Ask of me, and I will give You the nations for Your inheritance, and the farthest parts of the earth for Your possession.”

entries.originalText: And again He saith to Him, “Sit Thou at my right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool.”
entries.modernizedText: And again He says to Him, “Sit at my right hand, until I make Your enemies Your footstool.”

entries.originalText: But who are His enemies?
entries.modernizedText: But who are His enemies?

entries.originalText: All the wicked, and those who set themselves to oppose the will of God.
entries.modernizedText: All the wicked and those who set themselves against the will of God.

entries.originalText: Let us then, men and brethren, with all energy act the part of soldiers, in accordance with His holy commandments.
entries.modernizedText: Let us then, men and brethren, with all energy act as soldiers, in accordance with His holy commandments.

entries.originalText: Let us consider those who serve under our generals, with what order, obedience, and submissiveness they perform the things which are commanded them.
entries.modernizedText: Let us consider those who serve under our generals, and with what order, obedience, and submissiveness they perform the things commanded them.

entries.originalText: All are not prefects, nor commanders of a thousand, nor of a hundred, nor of fifty, nor the like, but each one in his own rank performs the things commanded by the king and the generals.
entries.modernizedText: Not all are prefects, commanders of a thousand, of a hundred, or of fifty, or the like, but each one in his own rank performs the things commanded by the king and the generals.

entries.originalText: The great cannot subsist without the small, nor the small without the great.
entries.modernizedText: The great cannot exist without the small, nor the small without the great.

entries.originalText: There is a kind of mixture in all things, and thence arises mutual advantage.
entries.modernizedText: There is a kind of mixture in all things, and from this arises mutual advantage.

entries.originalText: Let us take our body for an example.
entries.modernizedText: Let us take our body as an example.

entries.originalText: The head is nothing without the feet, and the feet are nothing without the head; yea, the very smallest members of our body are necessary and useful to the whole body.
entries.modernizedText: The head is nothing without the feet, and the feet are nothing without the head; indeed, the very smallest members of our body are necessary and useful to the whole body.

entries.originalText: But all work harmoniously together, and are under one common rule for the preservation of the whole body.
entries.modernizedText: But all work harmoniously together and are under one common rule for the preservation of the whole body.

entries.originalText: Let our whole body, then, be preserved in Christ Jesus; and let every one be subject to his neighbour, according to the special gift bestowed upon him.
entries.modernizedText: Let our whole body, then, be preserved in Christ Jesus, and let everyone be subject to his neighbor according to the special gift bestowed upon him.

entries.originalText: Let the strong not despise the weak, and let the weak show respect unto the strong.
entries.modernizedText: Let the strong not despise the weak, and let the weak show respect to the strong.

entries.originalText: Let the rich man provide for the wants of the poor; and let the poor man bless God, because He hath given him one by whom his need may be supplied.
entries.modernizedText: Let the rich man provide for the needs of the poor, and let the poor man bless God, because He has given him one by whom his need may be supplied.

entries.originalText: Let the wise man display his wisdom, not by [mere] words, but through good deeds.
entries.modernizedText: Let the wise man display his wisdom not through [mere] words but through good deeds.

entries.originalText: Let the humble not bear testimony to himself, but leave witness to be borne to him by another.
entries.modernizedText: Let the humble man not bear testimony to himself, but leave witness to be borne to him by another.

entries.originalText: Let him that is pure in the flesh not grow proud of it, and boast, knowing that it was another who bestowed on him the gift of continence.
entries.modernizedText: Let him who is pure in the flesh not grow proud of it or boast, knowing that another bestowed on him the gift of continence.

entries.originalText: Let us consider, then, brethren, of what matter we were made,—who and what manner of beings we came into the world, as it were out of a sepulchre, and from utter darkness.
entries.modernizedText: Let us consider, then, brethren, of what substance we were made—who we are and what kind of beings came into the world, as it were out of a sepulcher and from utter darkness.

entries.originalText: He who made us and fashioned us, having prepared His bountiful gifts for us before we were born, introduced us into His world.
entries.modernizedText: He who made and fashioned us, having prepared His bountiful gifts for us before we were born, introduced us into His world.

entries.originalText: Since, therefore, we receive all these things from Him, we ought for everything to give Him thanks; to whom be glory for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: Since, therefore, we receive all these things from Him, we ought to give Him thanks for everything; to Him be glory forever and ever.

entries.originalText: Foolish and inconsiderate men, who have neither wisdom nor instruction, mock and deride us, being eager to exalt themselves in their own conceits.
entries.modernizedText: Foolish and thoughtless men, who have neither wisdom nor instruction, mock and deride us, eager to exalt themselves in their own conceits.

entries.originalText: For what can a mortal man do, or what strength is there in one made out of the dust?
entries.modernizedText: For what can a mortal man do, or what strength is there in one made from dust?

entries.originalText: For it is written, “There was no shape before mine eyes, only I heard a sound, and a voice [saying], What then?
entries.modernizedText: For it is written, “There was no shape before my eyes; I heard only a sound and a voice [saying], What then?

entries.originalText: Shall a man be pure before the Lord?
entries.modernizedText: Shall a man be pure before the Lord?

entries.originalText: Or shall such an one be [counted] blameless in his deeds, seeing He does not confide in His servants, and has charged even His angels with perversity?
entries.modernizedText: Or shall such a one be [counted] blameless in his deeds, since He does not trust His servants and has charged even His angels with perversity?

entries.originalText: The heaven is not clean in His sight: how much less they that dwell in houses of clay, of which also we ourselves were made!
entries.modernizedText: The heavens are not clean in His sight; how much less those who dwell in houses of clay, from which we ourselves were also made!

entries.originalText: He smote them as a moth; and from morning even until evening they endure not.
entries.modernizedText: He struck them like a moth, and from morning until evening they do not endure.

entries.originalText: Because they could furnish no assistance to themselves, they perished.
entries.modernizedText: Because they could provide no help for themselves, they perished.

entries.originalText: He breathed upon them, and they died, because they had no wisdom.
entries.modernizedText: He breathed upon them, and they died because they had no wisdom.

entries.originalText: But call now, if any one will answer thee, or if thou wilt look to any of the holy angels; for wrath destroys the foolish man, and envy killeth him that is in error.
entries.modernizedText: But call now, if anyone will answer you, or if you will look to any of the holy angels; for wrath destroys the foolish man, and envy kills him who is in error.

entries.originalText: I have seen the foolish taking root, but their habitation was presently consumed.
entries.modernizedText: I have seen the foolish taking root, but their dwelling was quickly consumed.

entries.originalText: Let their sons be far from safety; let them be despised before the gates of those less than themselves, and there shall be none to deliver.
entries.modernizedText: Let their sons be far from safety; let them be despised before the gates of those lesser than themselves, and there will be no one to deliver them.

entries.originalText: For what was prepared for them, the righteous shall eat; and they shall not be delivered from evil.”
entries.modernizedText: For what was prepared for them, the righteous will eat, and they will not be delivered from evil.”

entries.originalText: These things therefore being manifest to us, and since we look into the depths of the divine knowledge, it behoves us to do all things in [their proper] order, which the Lord has commanded us to perform at stated times.
entries.modernizedText: Since these things are manifest to us and we look into the depths of divine knowledge, it behooves us to do all things in [their proper] order, which the Lord has commanded us to perform at stated times.

entries.originalText: He has enjoined offerings [to be presented] and service to be performed [to Him], and that not thoughtlessly or irregularly, but at the appointed times and hours.
entries.modernizedText: He has commanded offerings [to be presented] and service to be performed [to Him], not thoughtlessly or irregularly, but at the appointed times and hours.

entries.originalText: Where and by whom He desires these things to be done, He Himself has fixed by His own supreme will, in order that all things, being piously done according to His good pleasure, may be acceptable unto Him.
entries.modernizedText: Where and by whom He desires these things to be done, He Himself has fixed by His own supreme will, so that all things, being piously done according to His good pleasure, may be acceptable to Him.

entries.originalText: Those, therefore, who present their offerings at the appointed times, are accepted and blessed; for inasmuch as they follow the laws of the Lord, they sin not.
entries.modernizedText: Those, therefore, who present their offerings at the appointed times are accepted and blessed, for since they follow the laws of the Lord, they do not sin.

entries.originalText: For his own peculiar services are assigned to the high priest, and their own proper place is prescribed to the priests, and their own special ministrations devolve on the Levites.
entries.modernizedText: For his own particular services are assigned to the high priest, the priests are given their own proper place, and their own special ministrations are assigned to the Levites.

entries.originalText: The layman is bound by the laws that pertain to laymen.
entries.modernizedText: The layman is bound by the laws that pertain to laymen.

entries.originalText: Let every one of you, brethren, give thanks to God in his own order, living in all good conscience, with becoming gravity, and not going beyond the rule of the ministry prescribed to him.
entries.modernizedText: Let every one of you, brethren, give thanks to God in his own order, living with a good conscience and becoming seriousness, and not going beyond the rule of the ministry prescribed to him.

entries.originalText: Not in every place, brethren, are the daily sacrifices offered, or the peace-offerings, or the sin-offerings and the trespass-offerings, but in Jerusalem only.
entries.modernizedText: The daily sacrifices, peace offerings, sin offerings, and trespass offerings are not offered in every place, brethren, but only in Jerusalem.

entries.originalText: And even there they are not offered in any place, but only at the altar before the temple, that which is offered being first carefully examined by the high priest and the ministers already mentioned.
entries.modernizedText: And even there they are not offered in any place, but only at the altar before the temple; what is offered is first carefully examined by the high priest and the ministers already mentioned.

entries.originalText: Those, therefore, who do anything beyond that which is agreeable to His will, are punished with death.
entries.modernizedText: Those, therefore, who do anything beyond what is agreeable to His will are punished with death.

entries.originalText: Ye see, brethren, that the greater the knowledge that has been vouchsafed to us, the greater also is the danger to which we are exposed.
entries.modernizedText: You see, brethren, that the greater the knowledge granted to us, the greater also is the danger to which we are exposed.

entries.originalText: The apostles have preached the gospel to us from the Lord Jesus Christ; Jesus Christ [has done so] from God.
entries.modernizedText: The apostles preached the gospel to us from the Lord Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ [preached it] from God.

entries.originalText: Christ therefore was sent forth by God, and the apostles by Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Christ, therefore, was sent forth by God, and the apostles by Christ.

entries.originalText: Both these appointments, then, were made in an orderly way, according to the will of God.
entries.modernizedText: Both these appointments, then, were made in an orderly way, according to the will of God.

entries.originalText: Having therefore received their orders, and being fully assured by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, and established in the word of God, with full assurance of the Holy Ghost, they went forth proclaiming that the kingdom of God was at hand.
entries.modernizedText: Having received their orders, therefore, and being fully assured by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ and established in the word of God, with full assurance of the Holy Spirit, they went forth proclaiming that the kingdom of God was at hand.

entries.originalText: And thus preaching through countries and cities, they appointed the first fruits [of their labours], having first proved them by the Spirit, to be bishops and deacons of those who should afterwards believe.
entries.modernizedText: And preaching through countries and cities, they appointed the firstfruits [of their labors], having first tested them by the Spirit, to be bishops and deacons of those who would afterward believe.

entries.originalText: Nor was this any new thing, since indeed many ages before it was written concerning bishops and deacons.
entries.modernizedText: Nor was this anything new, since many ages earlier it was written concerning bishops and deacons.

entries.originalText: For thus saith the Scripture in a certain place, “I will appoint their bishops in righteousness, and their deacons in faith.”
entries.modernizedText: For thus says the Scripture in a certain place, “I will appoint their bishops in righteousness and their deacons in faith.”

entries.originalText: And what wonder is it if those in Christ who were entrusted with such a duty by God, appointed those [ministers] before mentioned, when the blessed Moses also, “a faithful servant in all his house,” noted down in the sacred books all the injunctions which were given him, and when the other prophets also followed him, bearing witness with one consent to the ordinances which he had appointed?
entries.modernizedText: And what wonder is it if those in Christ who were entrusted with such a duty by God appointed the [ministers] mentioned above, when the blessed Moses also, “a faithful servant in all his house,” recorded in the sacred books all the instructions given to him, and the other prophets also followed him, bearing unanimous witness to the ordinances he had appointed?

entries.originalText: For, when rivalry arose concerning the priesthood, and the tribes were contending among themselves as to which of them should be adorned with that glorious title, he commanded the twelve princes of the tribes to bring him their rods, each one being inscribed with the name of the tribe.
entries.modernizedText: For when rivalry arose concerning the priesthood and the tribes were contending among themselves over which of them should be honored with that glorious title, he commanded the twelve princes of the tribes to bring him their rods, each inscribed with the name of the tribe.

entries.originalText: And he took them and bound them [together], and sealed them with the rings of the princes of the tribes, and laid them up in the tabernacle of witness on the table of God.
entries.modernizedText: He took them and bound them [together], sealed them with the rings of the princes of the tribes, and laid them in the tabernacle of witness on the table of God.

entries.originalText: And having shut the doors of the tabernacle, he sealed the keys, as he had done the rods, and said to them, Men and brethren, the tribe whose rod shall blossom has God chosen to fulfil the office of the priesthood, and to minister unto Him.
entries.modernizedText: Having shut the doors of the tabernacle, he sealed the keys, as he had done the rods, and said to them, Men and brethren, the tribe whose rod blossoms is the one God has chosen to fulfill the office of the priesthood and minister to Him.

entries.originalText: And when the morning was come, he assembled all Israel, six hundred thousand men, and showed the seals to the princes of the tribes, and opened the tabernacle of witness, and brought forth the rods.
entries.modernizedText: When morning came, he assembled all Israel, six hundred thousand men, showed the seals to the princes of the tribes, opened the tabernacle of witness, and brought forth the rods.

entries.originalText: And the rod of Aaron was found not only to have blossomed, but to bear fruit upon it.
entries.modernizedText: And Aaron’s rod was found not only to have blossomed but also to bear fruit.

entries.originalText: What think ye, beloved?
entries.modernizedText: What do you think, beloved?

entries.originalText: Did not Moses know beforehand that this would happen?
entries.modernizedText: Did not Moses know beforehand that this would happen?

entries.originalText: Undoubtedly he knew; but he acted thus, that there might be no sedition in Israel, and that the name of the true and only God might be glorified; to whom be glory for ever and ever.
entries.modernizedText: Undoubtedly he knew, but he acted thus so that there might be no sedition in Israel and the name of the true and only God might be glorified; to Him be glory forever and ever.
